boot_command.note: runs the moment this node is ready, before the idle-grace clock matters; kill_command cancels it

custom_image.note: your own image, supervised by the platform: its entrypoint never runs (the platform keeps the node alive for run_command), and only the home path survives stops - everything else resets every wake

queue.arrival_note: Boot command cmd-8y9yk is set. It starts the moment the node is ready, even when you are not polling. get_command answers for it now. Do not delete this node to start over. Its files die with it and the boot command dies with this one, and the new node waits from zero.
queue.demand_note: QUEUE DEPTH STARTS MORE MACHINES. Your queued node's GPUs are a term in the fleet's own demand target, counted on the next procurement pass, so joining this queue is what makes the fleet grow and withdrawing makes it shrink. A full fleet is a reason to queue, not a reason to hold work back - queued time is free, your place is held to expires_at, and holding the work back is the one move that guarantees no machine is ever started for it. This is not a promise of a machine (a spend ceiling or a frozen market still binds, and capacity_inbound says whether one is coming for THIS entry) - it is the direction: a queue nobody joins starts nothing.
queue.estimate_basis: queue from 15 recent cpu-8 wake departures over 1d; spin-up from 3 cpu-8 wake samples; no recent wake history for this shape

priority.first_node_headstart_withheld: this org already holds a node that is running, coming up, or in its grace window, and the first-concurrent-node head start is the growth floor for an org holding NONE. A stopped (parked) node does not count. Nothing to do about it - this is the standard wait for this shape.

calendar.note: Fridays 33% off, weekends 20% off (US Pacific) - applied to the minutes that run on those days, not locked at create

resources.note: this container's cgroup budget - the CPU limit is a CFS quota, which os.cpu_count(), /proc/cpuinfo, psutil and free cannot see: they all report the HOST. Size parallelism (dataloader num_workers, multiprocessing.Pool, make -j) and memory to THESE numbers. Also inside the container: $GMN_CPU_LIMIT, $GMN_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES, with OMP_NUM_THREADS, RAYON_NUM_THREADS, MAX_JOBS and PYTHON_CPU_COUNT preset to the budget, so the OpenMP, Rust and torch-extension-build pools size to it. They are set on the CONTAINER, so they outrank an ENV baked into a custom image; override them in run_command's env, not a Dockerfile. GNU nproc answers the budget too (it reads OMP_NUM_THREADS) - busybox/Alpine nproc does not, so check yours on a custom image. What reports the host everywhere is os.cpu_count() (and PYTHON_CPU_COUNT only reaches it on Python 3.13+): read $GMN_CPU_LIMIT instead of os.cpu_count() anywhere you size a pool.
